_provenance: Real HID traffic captured 2026-08-11 from the vendor's own browser tool at yunzii-game.com (Picture Settings -> Upload pictures -> 'Save to the device') with fixtures/test-quadrants.png as the source image, using a sendReport hook of the same shape as scripts/capture-hook.js. These bytes were read out of the live page and written to this file by a script -- they were NEVER hand-typed, and they were NEVER read back from fixtures/picture-upload.json. fixtures/picture-upload.json is generated independently by scripts/build-fixtures.js, which re-derives all 552 reports from fixtures/test-quadrants.png through the documented protocol model; scripts/check-raw-consistency.js then compares the two byte for byte, so that check compares the MODEL against real HARDWARE evidence, not the model against itself.
source_image: fixtures/test-quadrants.png (160x96, exactly the panel size, so no resampling ambiguity)
direction_note: OUT reports only. The device's ACKs were not recorded in this capture, so none are invented here: earlier fixtures (page-switch, clear-picture) store ACKs constructed by flipping byte 6 from 0x00 to 0x55, which is a derived value rather than a fresh observation. Omitting them keeps this file purely observed data. 552 OUT reports is also exactly what the CLI produces, which is what the fixture needs to lock.
report_size_note: Each entry is the full 64-byte wire report. The vendor's JavaScript builds a 63-byte array and calls sendReport(0, data); Chrome zero-pads it to the output report size the device's own HID report descriptor declares. That descriptor was read from Linux sysfs (/sys/class/hidraw/*/device/report_descriptor) for this exact device and says Report Count = 64, Report Size = 8, with no Report ID item, for both the input and the output report. So the 64th byte is a real part of the report and is always 0x00 here; it is padding, not a transcription artifact.
structure: 1x start (0x40 cmd16) + 1x declare-size (0x41 cmd12) + 549x bulk (0x41) + 1x finish (0x42) = 552
